title: Bobby Deol and Anurag Kashyap Made a Film About #MeToo in the Age of Instagram — and It Premiered at TIFF Before Anyone in India Saw It
excerpt: Bandar drops its trailer May 21 and hits theatres worldwide June 5. For the diaspora, this is the kind of Indian cinema that actually matters.
body:
There is a specific kind of Bollywood film that makes NRIs sit up in their seats — not the ₹500 crore spectacle, not the family entertainer designed for Diwali weekends, but the dark, uncomfortable, morally ambiguous drama that reminds you Indian cinema can go places Hollywood is still afraid to touch.

Bandar is that film.

Directed by Anurag Kashyap and starring Bobby Deol in what might be the most interesting role of his career, Bandar tells the story of Samar — a fading television star whose fame is slipping through his fingers when his ex-girlfriend accuses him of rape after he cuts all contact with her. The accusation leads to his arrest and throws him into a legal system more interested in keeping him locked up than in finding the truth.

The film premiered at the Toronto International Film Festival in 2025, which means international audiences — including a significant chunk of the NRI community in North America — got a first look before anyone in India. That alone tells you something about where Kashyap sees this film sitting: not in the masala multiplex circuit, but in the global conversation about power, consent, and the weaponization of social media.

The Bobby Deol Nobody Expected

Five years ago, if someone told you Bobby Deol would become one of the most compelling actors in Indian cinema, you would have laughed. The man was a 90s heartthrob who drifted into irrelevance, showing up at parties but rarely on screen. Then came Animal in 2023, where his menacing, nearly silent antagonist earned him the internet-anointed title “Lord Bobby.” Suddenly, directors who had never considered him were calling.

Kashyap clearly sees something in Deol that most of Bollywood missed. The teaser, which dropped on May 7 and promptly went viral, shows him in a wild retro-rockstar avatar — think disco-era excess meets psychological unraveling. It is chaotic, visually dense, and unmistakably a Kashyap film. Sunny Deol publicly called his brother “Lord Bobby” in response to the teaser, which tells you even the family gets it now.

This is Bobby Deol’s first solo lead role in 17 years. Let that sink in.

The Team Behind the Story

The screenplay comes from Sudip Sharma and Abhishek Banerjee — the same team that built Paatal Lok, Kohrra, and Udta Punjab. If those names mean something to you, you already know this script will not pull its punches. The ensemble cast is equally stacked: Sanya Malhotra, Raj B Shetty, Sapna Pabbi, Saba Azad, Riddhi Sen, Jitendra Joshi, Indrajeet Sukumaran, and Nagesh Bhosle.

Produced by Nikhil Dwivedi’s Saffron Magicworks and backed by Zee Studios, Bandar is releasing worldwide on June 5, 2026 — meaning NRIs in the US, UK, and Canada should be able to catch it opening weekend at major multiplex chains that carry Indian releases.

Why the Diaspora Should Care

The #MeToo conversation in India has always been complicated — it arrived late, burned bright, and then seemingly vanished from public discourse without the systemic changes that followed in the West. For NRIs who watched that conversation unfold from abroad, often through the distorted lens of social media, Bandar offers something rare: a serious artistic engagement with the aftermath.

Kashyap has said the film is inspired by a real-life event. It does not take sides. It does not preach. It shows you a man whose life is destroyed by an accusation, and it asks you to sit with the discomfort of not knowing who to believe. That is the kind of storytelling that travels — and the TIFF premiere proved it.

The trailer drops May 21. If you have been waiting for Indian cinema to grow up and tackle the stories that actually matter, this is it.

Bandar releases in theatres worldwide on June 5, 2026.
